text:
toni: Heads-up: customers hitting import/runtime errors when using the JS SDK in edge runtimes. Example: "SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module" even though project is ESM.

qian: Are they bundling? Often bundlers or package `exports` resolve to a CJS entry. Can you share the import line and package.json `type`?

toni: Import is `import Inference from '@redwood/inference'`. package.json has "type": "module". Minimal edge route: ```js
import Inference from '@redwood/inference'
export default (req) => new Response('ok')
```
Error shows `require()` in a helper inside the SDK.

rafa: Short-term: import the ESM build path directly if published (e.g., `@redwood/inference/esm/index.mjs`) or add a bundler alias to force the esm entry. Long-term we need `exports.import` in package.json and `.d.ts` pointed at the ESM entry.

qian: Also note worker/edge differences: process.env is not reliable, pass apiKey explicitly or read from request headers. Add example in docs for header-based auth.

toni: Filing issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/js-sdk/issues/177 — requested: explicit `exports.import`, types for ESM, edge docs, and avoid top-level require().

devx-bot: Added label `sdk-edge` and linked docs page <https://redwood.inference/docs/js-sdk-edge>.

toni: I'll draft the docs snippet and a tiny repro repo. Thanks!
